Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering
Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering
Perform innovative research that advances electrical systems and devices.
Advance your career and become a leading researcher in academia or industry with a Ph.D. in electrical engineering from Northern Illinois University. Our program prepares you to conduct independent, high-impact research and turn innovative ideas into real-world solutions.
Develop deep expertise in your chosen specialization while honing your ability to solve complex engineering challenges. At NIU, you’ll build the skills needed to make meaningful contributions at local, national and global levels.

How Can Earning a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering Advance My Career?
A Ph.D. in electrical engineering positions you for leadership roles across sectors. Graduates are prepared for careers in:
Higher education and academic research
National and government laboratories
Federal and state agencies
Corporate research facilities
The program emphasizes the integration of advanced technical knowledge with practical application, equipping you to bridge the gap between research and innovation.
At a Glance
90 credit hours
In person
Full or part time
Start in the fall, spring or summer semester
Testimonials
I'm a Type 1 diabetic, so being able to provide to the world that kept me alive and to help people grow like me just makes me feel like I'm giving back....Thanks to NIU, I can immerse myself into this research that has given me a feeling of purpose.
Selina Cervantes, Ph.D. candidate, electrical engineering
I want my students to take away a lifelong learning habit that allows and motivates them to learn in the future. Electrical engineering is changing every day, and I would like my students to learn to be an engineer, act as an engineer and work as an engineer.
Lichuan Liu, professor, electrical engineering

How to Apply
You’ll apply through the Graduate School.
Application deadlines:
Fall: August 1 (May 1 for international applicants)
Spring: Dec. 10 (Oct. 1 for international applicants)
Summer: June 1
Application Materials
To be considered for admission, you must meet Graduate School requirements along with program-specific criteria:
A bachelor’s degree (B.S.) in electrical engineering or a related field
Minimum GPA of 3.00
Statement of purpose
Three letters of recommendation
Applicants from non–electrical engineering backgrounds are welcome and may be required to complete foundational coursework as part of the program.
Apply to the Graduate School
Costs and Funding
Our competitive tuition and fees help ensure an excellent return on the investment of your time and resources. Learn about CEET scholarships and additional funding opportunities for graduate students.
Curriculum and Requirements
At 90 credits, it will take approximately two to three years to complete your degree.
View Program Requirements
View Coursework
Faculty
Our faculty bring diverse experiences and backgrounds across electrical engineering. They have expertise in microelectronic fabrication, signal processing, electromagnetics, among other fields. They’re committed to supporting and collaborating with students in their scholarly and research endeavors. View current faculty research projects.
